objective: Close the cross-project identity gap in immutable Vercel deployment evidence.
selection_basis: R-022 is the highest-priority frontier item whose remaining deployment-identity acceptance path exposed a non-duplicative fail-open condition in the committed v1 validator.
completed_slices: Compared the committed v1 validator against current Vercel v13 response fields.
Identified that presence-only project identity and commit-only Git source matching can accept a deployment from the wrong Vercel project or GitHub repository.
Implemented v2 requiring trusted expected projectId, project name, GitHub repoId, ref, and commit SHA.
Added six deterministic tests covering exact acceptance, wrong project, wrong repository, wrong ref, incomplete expected identity, and canonical digest stability.
Retained source status, uncertainty, evidence strength, claim boundary, and falsification routes.
acceptance_remaining: Integrate v2 ahead of V-001 deployment promotion while retaining v1 only for historical compatibility.
Source the expected Vercel project ID from trusted configuration or authenticated project metadata, never from the deployment object being validated.
Fetch and retain one authenticated Vercel v13 deployment object after provider capacity returns.
Run v2 against the retained object and independently verify project metadata and generated hostname behavior.
safe_next_action: Wire v2 into the V-001 assessor with explicit trusted expected identity inputs; fail closed when any expected project, repository, ref, or commit field is absent or mismatched. Do not initiate a deployment while provider capacity remains blocked.
